concepts.name: Living organisms exhibit coordinated characteristics such as growth, reproduction, metabolism, cellular organisation and response to stimuli
learning_points: Understand defining characteristics of living organisms
Understand consciousness and response to stimuli

concepts.name: Life exhibits enormous diversity that requires systematic organisation and classification
Organisms are arranged in a hierarchy of taxonomic categories based on shared characteristics
Taxonomic aids provide preserved specimens, records and identification tools for studying biodiversity
Monerans are prokaryotic organisms with diverse cellular and nutritional characteristics
Protists are predominantly unicellular eukaryotic organisms with diverse modes of nutrition and movement
Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotes characterised by absorptive nutrition and diverse reproductive structures
Plants and animals represent major multicellular eukaryotic lineages with distinct organisational and nutritional patterns
Some biological entities do not fit conventional cellular kingdom classification
Algae are predominantly aquatic photosynthetic organisms with diverse pigments and body forms
Bryophytes are non-vascular plants whose reproduction depends on water
Pteridophytes possess vascular tissues but reproduce through spores rather than seeds
Gymnosperms produce exposed ovules and seeds that are not enclosed within fruits
Angiosperms are flowering plants in which ovules are enclosed within an ovary and seeds develop inside fruits
learning_points: Distinguish monocots and dicots at the required level

concepts.name: Plants alternate between haploid gametophytic and diploid sporophytic generations
learning_points: Compare life cycles of major plant groups

concepts.name: Animal classification considers levels of organisation, symmetry, germ layers, coelom, segmentation and notochord
learning_points: Understand acoelomate, pseudocoelomate and coelomate conditions

concepts.name: Non-chordate animals show diverse body plans and adaptations
Chordates possess characteristic structures including notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal openings at some stage
Vertebrates are classified into major classes based on body organisation, habitat and evolutionary characteristics
Roots anchor plants, absorb water and minerals and may become specialised for storage and support
Stems support aerial parts and conduct materials while showing diverse structural modifications
Leaves are specialised photosynthetic organs with characteristic arrangements and venation patterns
Inflorescence describes the arrangement of flowers on the floral axis
Flowers are reproductive structures composed of specialised whorls
Fruits generally develop from ovaries after fertilisation and may show diverse structures
Seeds contain an embryo and stored resources protected by specialised coverings
Important plant families can be recognised by characteristic vegetative, floral and fruit features
Plant tissues are organised groups of cells specialised for growth, support, transport and other functions
Simple permanent tissues consist of structurally similar cells with specialised functions
Complex vascular tissues transport water, minerals and organic nutrients through plants
Plant tissues are organised into tissue systems that perform integrated functions
learning_points: Relate tissue systems to plant organs

concepts.name: Roots and stems have characteristic tissue arrangements that support absorption, transport and growth
Leaf tissues are organised for photosynthesis, gas exchange and transport
Secondary growth increases the girth of many woody plants through lateral meristem activity
Animal tissues are organised groups of cells specialised for protection, support, movement, secretion and coordination
Epithelial tissues cover body surfaces and line cavities and organs
Connective tissues bind, support, protect and transport substances
Muscle tissue contracts to produce movement
Nervous tissue receives, processes and transmits information
Representative animals demonstrate specialised organ systems and body organisation
The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of life
learning_points: Understand historical development of cell theory
Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level

concepts.name: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and have a relatively simple internal organisation
Eukaryotic cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus and specialised membrane-bound organelles
Cell organelles perform specialised functions while operating as an integrated system
The nucleus contains genetic material and coordinates cellular activities
Cytoskeletal and surface structures maintain cell shape, organisation and movement
The plasma membrane is a dynamic lipid-protein structure controlling exchange between cell and environment
The plant cell wall provides mechanical support and protection outside the plasma membrane
Carbohydrates are organic molecules with major structural and energy-storage roles
Proteins are polymers of amino acids folded into structures that determine biological function
learning_points: Classify amino acids at the required level

concepts.name: Lipids are hydrophobic or amphipathic biomolecules important in energy storage and membrane structure
Nucleic acids store, transmit and express genetic information
Enzymes are biological catalysts that accelerate reactions by lowering activation energy
learning_points: Understand enzyme inhibition at the required level

concepts.name: Cells contain numerous low-molecular-weight metabolites essential for cellular processes
learning_points: Understand amino acids as metabolic intermediates

concepts.name: The cell cycle coordinates growth, DNA replication and cell division
learning_points: Relate cell-cycle phases to cellular events

concepts.name: Mitosis produces daughter cells with chromosome numbers equivalent to the parent cell
Meiosis reduces chromosome number and generates genetic variation in sexually reproducing organisms
Mitosis and meiosis differ in number of divisions, chromosome behaviour, products and biological roles
Plant cells exchange substances through passive and active transport mechanisms
Water movement is governed by differences in water potential across membranes
Vascular tissues transport water, minerals and organic solutes over long distances
learning_points: Distinguish ascent of sap and translocation

concepts.name: Water rises through xylem through mechanisms involving root pressure, cohesion and transpiration
Transpiration is loss of water vapour from aerial plant parts, mainly through stomata
learning_points: Understand antitranspirant concept at the required level

concepts.name: Organic solutes are translocated through phloem from sources to sinks using pressure-driven bulk flow
Certain mineral elements are essential for normal plant growth and completion of the life cycle
Mineral elements participate in structural, metabolic and regulatory functions
Deficiency of essential minerals produces characteristic effects on plant growth and metabolism
Hydroponics allows plants to grow in nutrient solutions without soil
learning_points: Understand its use in studying mineral nutrition

concepts.name: Plants acquire nitrogen through nitrate or ammonium forms while microorganisms contribute to biological nitrogen fixation
Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy while synthesising organic molecules from carbon dioxide and water
Photosynthetic pigments absorb specific wavelengths of light and transfer excitation energy to reaction centres
Light-dependent reactions generate ATP and reducing power through photosynthetic electron transport
The Calvin cycle uses ATP and reducing power to convert fixed carbon into carbohydrate precursors
learning_points: Understand requirement of ATP and NADPH

concepts.name: Photorespiration occurs when RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase and leads to loss of fixed carbon
C4 plants concentrate carbon dioxide around RuBisCO to reduce photorespiration
Photosynthetic rate depends on environmental and internal factors that can become limiting
Cellular respiration releases usable energy from organic molecules through controlled oxidation reactions
Glycolysis converts glucose into pyruvate through a sequence of cytoplasmic reactions
Fermentation regenerates NAD+ when oxygen is unavailable and produces incompletely oxidised products
Aerobic respiration completely oxidises pyruvate through acetyl-CoA formation, Krebs cycle and electron transport
Complete oxidation of a respiratory substrate yields ATP through substrate-level and oxidative phosphorylation
learning_points: Recognise factors affecting actual cellular ATP yield

concepts.name: Respiratory pathways provide both energy and metabolic intermediates for biosynthesis
Respiratory quotient compares carbon dioxide evolved with oxygen consumed during respiration
learning_points: Determine RQ for fats and proteins at the required level

concepts.name: Plant growth is an irreversible increase in size accompanied by coordinated cellular changes
Plant development involves coordinated processes of growth, differentiation, maturation and senescence
Plant hormones regulate growth and development at very low concentrations
learning_points: Relate hormones to major physiological effects

concepts.name: Some plants regulate flowering in response to relative durations of light and darkness
Exposure to low temperature can induce or promote flowering in certain plants
Seed germination begins when suitable environmental conditions activate metabolic and developmental processes
The human digestive system mechanically and chemically processes food before absorption
Digestive glands secrete enzymes and other substances that facilitate breakdown of food
Macromolecular nutrients are enzymatically broken into absorbable units
learning_points: Understand nucleic-acid digestion at the required level

concepts.name: Digested nutrients cross intestinal epithelium and enter blood or lymph
learning_points: Understand absorption of fatty acids and glycerol
Understand transport through blood and lymph

concepts.name: Absorbed nutrients are utilised by tissues while undigested material is eliminated
Disruption of digestion or absorption can produce characteristic gastrointestinal disorders
learning_points: Recognise causes and basic preventive measures

concepts.name: The respiratory system conducts air to gas-exchange surfaces where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged
Breathing occurs through coordinated changes in thoracic volume and pressure
Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across respiratory surfaces according to partial-pressure gradients
Blood transports oxygen mainly through haemoglobin and carbon dioxide in several dissolved and chemically bound forms
Respiratory volumes and capacities quantify air movement through the lungs
Respiratory function can be impaired by infections, allergens, smoking and other environmental factors
learning_points: Understand occupational respiratory disorders at the required level

concepts.name: Blood is a connective tissue that transports gases, nutrients, hormones and wastes while supporting defence and regulation
Blood groups are determined by specific antigens and antibodies and are important in transfusion compatibility
Blood clotting prevents excessive blood loss through a coordinated cascade involving platelets and clotting factors
The cardiovascular system circulates blood through a four-chambered heart and interconnected vessels
The cardiac cycle consists of coordinated atrial and ventricular contractions and relaxations
An electrocardiogram records electrical activity associated with cardiac cycles
learning_points: Relate ECG components to cardiac events

concepts.name: In humans, blood passes through the heart twice during one complete circuit of the body
learning_points: Understand separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

concepts.name: Disorders of blood vessels, heart and blood pressure can impair circulation
Metabolism produces nitrogenous and other wastes that must be eliminated to maintain internal balance
The human urinary system removes metabolic wastes and regulates water, ions and acid-base balance
The nephron performs filtration, reabsorption and secretion to form urine
Urine formation involves selective filtration of blood followed by regulated reabsorption and secretion
learning_points: Understand counter-current mechanism at the required level

concepts.name: Kidneys maintain osmotic and ionic balance through regulated water and solute handling
learning_points: Understand hormonal control of urine concentration

concepts.name: Kidney dysfunction can disturb waste removal and fluid-electrolyte balance
learning_points: Recognise transplant as a treatment option

concepts.name: Movement can occur at cellular or organismal levels through specialised structures and coordinated tissues
The human skeleton provides support, protection and sites for muscle attachment
Skeletal muscles contract through interactions between actin and myosin filaments
Muscle contraction occurs when actin filaments slide relative to myosin filaments using ATP-dependent cross-bridge cycling

topics.name: Disorders of muscular and skeletal systems

concepts.name: Musculoskeletal disorders can affect bones, joints and muscles
The nervous system coordinates rapid communication and responses through neurons and neural circuits
Neurons receive, integrate and transmit electrical and chemical signals
Nerve impulses arise from rapid changes in membrane potential caused by ion movements
Signals cross most synapses through neurotransmitter release and receptor activation
A reflex is a rapid, automatic response mediated through a neural pathway
The brain integrates sensory information, controls movement and regulates complex physiological and cognitive functions
Sensory receptors detect specific forms of environmental or internal stimuli
The endocrine system coordinates physiological processes through hormones released into body fluids
The hypothalamus and pituitary coordinate many endocrine functions through releasing hormones and tropic hormones
learning_points: Relate pituitary hormones to target glands

concepts.name: Thyroid and parathyroid hormones regulate metabolism, growth and calcium balance
Adrenal hormones participate in stress responses, metabolism, electrolyte balance and cardiovascular regulation
Pancreatic hormones maintain blood glucose homeostasis
Gonadal hormones regulate reproductive development and physiological functions
Abnormal hormone secretion or action can disturb physiological homeostasis
learning_points: Understand adrenal disorders at the required level
